### Summary

A passing CUDA build does not mean every feature was exercised on the GPU. The C++ tests built on the device fixture
run on both devices. A Python test runs on CUDA only when it moves its tensors there, and most Python test files do
not. This section names the files that test on both devices, the files that test on CPU only, and two kinetics
features that the suite checks on the CPU alone: the Kessler-form evaporation and the pressure switch.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Which assertions also run on CUDA, and which run on CPU only.

**Data.** The test files and the device each one uses.

**Placement.** Read after @sec-ch13-results.

**Activation.** A Python test runs on CUDA only if it moves its tensors there.

**Guarantee / limits.** 14 of 40 Python test files use CUDA; Kessler evaporation and the pressure switch are CPU-only.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

### Derivation

No derivation: this scheme is an inventory.

### Numerical method

No numerical method. The inventory is built in two steps:

1. Every C++ test built on `DeviceTest` ({{< code tests/device_testing.hpp DeviceTest >}}) runs on CPU and CUDA
   (@sec-ch13-suite).
2. A Python test file counts as covering CUDA when it names the CUDA device. Of the 40 Python test files, 14 do:
   `test_atm2d.py`, `test_cuda_workspace.py`, `test_evaporation_general.py`, `test_kinetics_base_units.py`,
   `test_kinetics_null_options.py`, `test_reaction_equilibrium.py`, `test_saturation_failure_reported.py`,
   `test_species_registry.py`, `test_thermo_default_nucleation.py`, `test_thermo_none_nucleation.py`,
   `test_thermo_none_nucleation_after_reset.py`, `test_thermo_x_warm_start_shape.py`,
   `test_thermo_y_none_nucleation.py` and `test_warm_start_shape.py`.[^ch13-coverage-grep]

: Device coverage of selected tests. {#tbl-ch13-device-coverage-tests}

Neither `test_evaporation_kessler.py` nor `test_coagulation_pressure_switch.py` names a device, so both run on CPU
only, on every build. Both pass on the CPU and the CUDA builds of @sec-ch13-results. A separate run outside the
suite fed their two reaction sets through the kinetics step on both devices. The rates, the Jacobian and the
implicit step agreed between CPU and CUDA to below $10^{-15}$ relative, that is, at round-off in double
precision.[^ch13-coverage-probe] The run and its table are in @sec-ch12, in the device dispatch section.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- **No suite test checks the Kessler form or the pressure switch on CUDA.** A CUDA-only regression in either would
  pass the suite. Adding a CUDA case to each file closes the gap.
:::

- The inventory counts a file as CUDA-covering if it names the device anywhere. Which assertions inside it run on
  CUDA is not tabulated yet. TODO.
- 26 of 40 Python test files name no CUDA device. Which of their features also run on CUDA through another test is
  not tabulated. TODO.
